Standard deviation can be used as a measure of spread
particularly important when we consider normally distributed data
, i.e. has a symmetrical ‘bell-curved’ shape with data becoming less concentrated further away from the mean.
For example, heights in a population tend to be ‘normally distributed’.
Standard deviation is the root mean square distance from the mean. For normally distributed heights, approximately 68% lie within one standard deviation of the mean.
